pages.lesson:
LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: PARAGRAPH WRITING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Writing 3.7 Guided Writing: Creative Writing (2 sessions) • Neatness and legibil
Topic 3.9: Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we need to keep household items safe?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. construct simple sentences to express ideas related to the theme
2. create a coherent paragraph for comprehension

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GUIDED WRITING: PARAGRAPH WRITING
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing helps you succeed in ARABIC LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GUIDED WRITING: PARAGRAPH WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Construct simple sentences to express ideas related to the theme

What this means
In this part you learn to construct simple sentences to express ideas related to the theme. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: construct simple sentences to express ideas related to the theme.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can construct simple sentences to express ideas related to the theme. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Create a coherent paragraph for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to create a coherent paragraph for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create a coherent paragraph for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create a coherent paragraph for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: construct simple sentences to express ideas related to the theme)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing to a partner. (skill: create a coherent paragraph for comprehension)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: construct simple sentences to express ideas related to the theme.
3. Practise this skill: create a coherent paragraph for comprehension.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we need to keep household items safe?
2. How does lack of coherence affect meaning in language?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: construct simple sentences to express ideas related to the theme.
5. Be able to: create a coherent paragraph for comprehension.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
